To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the financial crisis has an impact on firms in the whole chain.
the trade credit and bank credits of firms during financial crises are related to each other and they are affected from financial crisis.
trade credit behavior of firms is affected by the demand fall generated by the financial crisis and bank credit behavior is affected by trade credit behavior of the firm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
trade credit and bank relationship in supply chain during crisis and the impact of crisis on this relationship.
the trade credit and bank relationship during the financial crisis.
the impact of financial crisis on firms in a supply chain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trade credit is an alternative financing source during financial crisis.
the trade credit and bank credits are the main sources of supply chain financing during financial crises and firms are motivated to use these sources to maintain their relationships.
firms in the supply chains are affected by the financial crisis in a different way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
firms are motivated to provide trade credits in order not to loss their customers, and this situation is also supported by financial institutions.
trade credit behavior of firms is not only determined by the financial position of firms but also by the financial position and trade credit behavior of their customers.

the trade and bank credits are used by the firms as a financing source during financial crises and the firms are motivated to increase trade credit in order to keep the demand and bank credit in order to survive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trade credit and bank credits are not substitutes but complements during financial crisis.
the trade credit behavior of firms depends on the trade credit behavior and bank credit behavior on their customers.
trade credit and bank credits are complementary to each other and both of these credits have an impact on the survival of the firms during financial crises.
